# E.03A - More Than the Sum of Its Parts

## When Does Life Appear?

A membrane is not alive.

DNA is not alive.

Proteins are not alive.

Neither are water, sugars or fats.

Yet when all of these parts work together in a highly organized way, a living cell emerges.

Life is not a special ingredient—it is a remarkable property that emerges when many non-living components interact in the right way.
